title: Exploring The Effect of TikTok Trigger Warnings in a Clinical Sample of Youth at Risk of Suicide
official: Red Flag, Green Light: Exploring The Effect of TikTok Trigger Warnings in a Clinical Sample of Youth at Risk of Suicide
summary: Rates of suicide among Canadian youth have risen steadily over the past two decades, alongside rapid growth in social media use-especially TikTok. Our research shows that TikTok contains substantial suicide-related content that may pose risks to vulnerable young people by provoking distress or encouraging copycat behaviour. Many creators add trigger warnings (TWs) to flag upsetting material, yet their impact is unclear. Although research shows mixed effects of TWs among people with trauma histories, no studies have examined TWs in the context of suicide-related content. Our recent findings indicate that TWs are associated with reduced engagement suicide-related videos on TikTok-contrary to our hypothesis that they might increase engagement. Although we can only speculate, reduced engagement may reflect youth avoiding TW-labelled content, or other unknown factors. This study will examine how a clinical population of youth at risk of suicide emotionally and behaviourally respond to TWs on self-harm and suicide-related content. Findings will provide key evidence to inform public health recommendations aimed at protecting youth from harmful content online.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Lifetime or recent suicidal thoughts as measured on the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS)20 screening version. Defined as answering "YES" Question 2 on the C-SSRS with a lifetime and/or past month time-framing ("In your entire life, have you ever had any thoughts of killing yourself?" and/or "In the past month, have you had any thoughts of killing yourself?")
* Self-identified consumer of short-form content on social media (e.g. Instagram reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts) in the last year.
* English comprehension

Exclusion Criteria:

* Suicidal ideation with any intent or plan in the last 6 months. Defined as answering "YES" on any one C-SSRS Question 3 to 5 with a past 6-months timeframe. Note: Suicidal ideation in the absence of intent or planning is not an exclusion criterion
* Suicidal behaviour in the last 6 months. Defined as answering "YES" to C-SSRS Question 6 ("In your entire life, have you ever done anything, started to do anything, or prepared to do anything to end your life?") AND a 6-months follow up questions ("Was this within the past 6 months?"). Note: Lifetime suicidal behaviour (i.e. answering yes to only Question 6) is not an exclusion criterion
* In active psychosis or mania, as indicated by patient's medical records
